arxiv-2102-05416.title: Dynamic susceptibilities in dense soft athermal spheres under a finite-rate shear
arxiv-2102-05416.creator: Norihiro Oyama, Takeshi Kawasaki, Kuniyasu Saitoh
arxiv-2102-05416.description: Abstract The mechanical responses of dense packings of soft athermal spheres under a finite-rate shear are studied by means of molecular dynamics simulations. We investigate the volume fraction and shear rate dependence of the fluctuations in the shear stress and the interparticle contact number.

arxiv-2209-03357.title: Distilling Deep RL Models Into Interpretable Neuro-Fuzzy Systems
arxiv-2209-03357.creator: Arne Gevaert, Jonathan Peck and Yvan Saeys
arxiv-2209-03357.description: Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning uses a deep neural network to encode a policy, which achieves very good performance in a wide range of applications but is widely regarded as a black box model. A more interpretable alternative to deep networks is given by neuro-fuzzy controllers.

arxiv-2401-07359.title: Reliability and Interpretability in Science and Deep Learning
arxiv-2401-07359.creator: Luigi Scorzato
arxiv-2401-07359.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Luigi Scorzato. In recent years, the question of the reliability of Machine Learning (ML) methods has acquired significant importance, and the analysis of the associated uncertainties has motivated a growing amount of research. However, most of these studies have applied standard error analysis to ML models—and in particular Deep Neural Network (DNN) models—which represent a rather significant departure from standard scientific modelling.

arxiv-2406-00519.title: Learning Discrete Concepts in Latent Hierarchical Models
arxiv-2406-00519.creator: Lingjing Kong, Guangyi Chen, Biwei Huang, Eric P. Xing, Yuejie Chi, Kun Zhang
arxiv-2406-00519.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lingjing Kong, Guangyi Chen, Biwei Huang, Eric P. Xing, Yuejie Chi, Kun Zhang. Learning concepts from natural high-dimensional data (e.g., images) holds potential in building human-aligned and interpretable machine learning models. Despite its encouraging prospect, formalization and theoretical insights into this crucial task are still lacking.

arxiv-2502-13701.title: Causes and Strategies in Multiagent Systems
arxiv-2502-13701.creator: Sylvia S. Kerkhove, Natasha Alechina, Mehdi Dastani
arxiv-2502-13701.description: Abstract . Causality plays an important role in daily processes, human reasoning, and artificial intelligence. There has however not been much research on causality in multi-agent strategic settings. In this work, we introduce a systematic way to build a multi-agent system model, represented as a concurrent game structure, for a given structural causal model.

arxiv-2503-19139.title: Constraints of extended gravity theory in the regime of Universe accelerated extension: turnaround radius Constraints of extended gravity theory …
arxiv-2503-19139.description: Abstract Аннотация Applying the definition of the turnaround radius and the fact that the best agreement with observational data on extragalactic scales is currently provided by general relativity with the cosmological constant we consider the behaviour of spherically symmetric solutions of the Horndeski and Dvali-Gabadadze-Poratti models on these scales.

arxiv-2512-05374.title: Please Don’t Kill My Vibe
arxiv-2512-05374.creator: Charlie Summers, Haneen Mohammed, Eugene Wu
arxiv-2512-05374.description: Abstract . The promise of Large Language Model (LLM) agents is to perform complex, stateful tasks. This promise is stunted by significant risks—policy violations, process corruption, and security flaws—that stem from the lack of visibility and mechanisms to manage undesirable data flows produced by agent actions. Today, agent workflows are responsible for enforcing these policies in ad hoc ways.

arxiv-2601-01416.title: AirSpatialBot: A Spatially-Aware Aerial Agent for Fine-Grained Vehicle Attribute Recognization and Retrieval Thanks: * Correspondence author. Thanks: Yue Zhou, Ran Ding, Xue Jiang and Xingzhao Liu are with the Department of Electronic Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai 200240, Chin
arxiv-2601-01416.creator: Yue Zhou, Ran Ding, Xue Yang
arxiv-2601-01416.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yue Zhou, Ran Ding, Xue Yang. Despite notable advancements in remote sensing vision-language models (VLMs), existing models often struggle with spatial understanding, limiting their effectiveness in real-world applications. To push the boundaries of VLMs in remote sensing, we specifically address vehicle imagery captured by drones and introduce a spatially-aware dataset AirSpatial, which comprises over 206K instructions and introduces two novel tasks: Spatial Grounding and Spatial Question Answering. It is also the first remote sensing grounding dataset to provide 3DBB.

pmc-11610137.title: TRIM4 enhances small-molecule-induced neddylated-degradation of CORO1A for triple negative breast cancer therapy
pmc-11610137.creator: Wen-Jie Gu, Xiao-Xia Liu, Yi-Wen Shen, Yi-Ting Gong, Yi-Li Chen, Jiayi Lin, Dong Lu, Li-Jun Zhang, Hong-Zhuan Chen, Yi Jin, Zha-Jun Zhan, Wei-Dong Zhang, Jin-Mei Jin, Xin Luan
pmc-11610137.description: Background: As a critical member of the Coronin family, Coronin 1A (CORO1A) plays a crucial role in the progression of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, CORO1A is typically considered “undruggable” due to its smooth surface and complex protein-protein interactions (PPIs). Molecular glues have emerged as one of the most effective strategies to rapidly degrade such “undruggable” targets.

pmc-12568352.title: Recent advances in training intensity distribution theory for cyclic endurance sports: theoretical foundations, model comparisons, and periodization characteristics
pmc-12568352.creator: Qihao Sun, Yin Yu, Jiayue Cui, Simin Lin, Xiaohan Wang, Tian Zhou
pmc-12568352.description: Training Intensity Distribution (TID) has emerged as a crucial component of training load regulation, providing a critical foundation for designing endurance training programs and optimizing performance. This paper systematically reviews the theoretical underpinnings of TID and the evolution of training intensity zone classification.

pmc-12974810.title: Strategies for updating rules driven by reinforcement learning to solve social dilemmas
pmc-12974810.creator: Yang Wang, Xingchen Yu, Shounan Lu
pmc-12974810.description: This study incorporates historical performance into traditional imitation rules and proposes a moderated strategy update rule. In this framework, an individual’s temporal historical performance is calculated using the BM model. By adjusting the parameter δ, the influence of historical performance on strategy learning is determined, and the evolution of cooperation is subsequently observed.

pmc-13091336.title: Comparison of dominant foodborne and inhalant allergies developing in the first 5 years of life☆
pmc-13091336.creator: Qingxiu Xu, Qing Jiang, Yaqi Yang, Wenjing Li, Dongxia Ma, Wei Zhang, Rongfei Zhu, Lin Yang
pmc-13091336.description: BackgroundDuring the first 5 years of life, atopic individuals may develop cutaneous or respiratory symptoms with foodborne or airborne allergens. The route and dose of exposure are associated with sensitization. However, limited studies compare food and airborne allergies in these children.

pmc-13255280.title: Severe leptospirosis complicated by atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, myocarditis, and acute liver injury: a therapeutic challenge—a case report and review of the literature
pmc-13255280.creator: Risly NMM, Jayasinghe IK, Athauda N, Wevage KAD, Sahana JF
pmc-13255280.description: BackgroundSevere leptospirosis, also known as Weil’s disease, is a life-threatening zoonotic infection characterized by multi-organ dysfunction, including acute kidney injury and jaundice. We report this case due to its rarity and complex nature.Case presentationThis case report describes a 44-year-old previously healthy, Sri Lankan Sinhalese male who presented with high-grade fever, deep jaundice, acute kidney injury, and signs of systemic inflammation.

pmc-13327435.title: Evaluating the Influence of Injury‐Induced Microstructural Variations on the Efficacy of a Diffusion MRI‐Derived Axon Diameter Surrogate
pmc-13327435.creator: Hannah E Alderson, Chaoqi Mu, Li Min Chen, Mark D Does, Kevin D Harkins
pmc-13327435.description: PurposeTo investigate the utility of a recently demonstrated diffusion MRI derived axon diameter surrogate measure (∆D ⟂) under pathologic conditions induced by a spinal cord injury model.MethodsContusion injuries were performed on the thoracic–lumbar spinal cord of adult male rats. Eight weeks post‐injury, rats were sacrificed and their spinal cords imaged by MRI and then scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

pmc-13380739.title: Decoding urbanization pathways: An integrative land use change indicator framework for sustainable development in Nusantara
pmc-13380739.creator: Achmad Ghozali, Walter Timo de Vries
pmc-13380739.description: SummaryIndonesia’s new capital, Nusantara, is generating urban expansion that extends beyond administrative boundaries, yet its cross-boundary land-use dynamics remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a contextualized predictive-preventive framework of land use change (LUC) indicators for future urbanization assessment in the Nusantara agglomeration through a review-based conceptual synthesis.

pmc-13466972.title: Mediators of the Pain–Depression Relationship in Adults with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analyses
pmc-13466972.creator: Michael Tenti, Stefania Proietti, Corrado Fagnani, Emanuela Medda, Letizia Sampaolo, Laura Camoni, Federica Cilenti, Giorgia Varallo, Valentina Malafoglia, William Raffaeli, Virgilia Toccaceli
pmc-13466972.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Pain intensity and depressive symptoms are closely associated in adults with chronic pain (CP), contributing to greater disability, poorer treatment outcomes, and increased healthcare costs. However, the mechanisms underlying this symptom-level relationship remain incompletely understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to (i) identify all candidate factors mediating the effect of pain intensity on depressive symptoms, or vice versa, in adults with CP and (ii) estimate the magnitude of indirect, direct and total effects reported across eligible studies.
